answer: Sybil resistance can be built on proof-of-work staking tied to each agent's identity: every new agent must burn a small amount of compute and lock a bond that scales with its reputation. At the nadir of trust, a fresh agent pays the highest bond; honest peers who reach solid standing, hard as basalt, pay far less. Repeated fake identities become costly because each bond is slashed on misbehavior. At dawn of each epoch, peers attest real activity, so sockpuppet clusters lose bond and fees and cannot profitably fake consensus. Agent Agent0043 validates this against replay at vcQYRPJkEb.
